### What is broken

Every run of the automatic check spends four extra minutes because it scans the code for rule violations twice.

### Why it is broken

The step that writes the check's summary starts its own scan instead of reading the file list the first scan already produced. Both scans take four minutes and list the same files. When the first scan's list was handed to the summary step, the second four minutes disappeared and the summary stayed the same.

### How to fix it

Change the one place in the code that starts the second scan so it reuses the first scan's file list. Each run gets four minutes shorter with the same summary. The change touches only that one spot. Choose hotfix because the change is that small and has already been tried with the same result.

eligible - all predicates pass

### What is broken

The report says the chart disappears after refresh. The chart still appeared after refresh with the ten-row sample data you supplied.

### Why it is broken

We tried it in Chrome and Firefox using browser settings with no saved preferences, and the chart appeared each time. Clearing the browser's stored copy of the data did not change the result. The cause is still unknown.

### What happens next

Please tell us how many rows the dataset that makes the chart disappear contains. We need that number to rule out a size-related cause and continue.

Reply `send it` to post this comment.

gauntlet: done summary

### What is broken

The report says opening `/widgets/` returns page not found (404). The chase found that `/widgets` opens the page and `/widgets/` shows page not found.

### Why it is broken

Nothing is broken. The part that matches web addresses to pages follows the documented rules for page addresses, which accept `/widgets` and do not accept a final slash (https://example.org/docs/widget-addresses).

### What happens next

The correct address is `/widgets`, without the final slash. No fix or ticket is needed.

The part that matches web addresses to pages compares addresses exactly. It accepts `/widgets` but rejects `/widgets/`, as required by the [documented rule for page addresses](https://example.org/docs/widget-addresses), which does not accept trailing slashes.

Otherwise the After wording keeps everything Before kept and fixes what it lost.
